about: The country's and the world's yearly CO2, the base the climate engine's carbon laws move, and the path the rest of the world follows.

usEnergyCo2GtPerYear.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, U.S. energy-related carbon dioxide emissions, 2024 total 4,789 million metric tons (eia.gov/environment/emissions/carbon/).

worldFossilPath.spread: IEA's current-policies scenario stays near the 2024 level to 2050 (about 38 Gt, the high end); its stated-policies scenario ends below 30 Gt in 2050.
worldFossilPath.source: 2025: Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Global Carbon Project, Nov 2025), "projects 38.1 billion tonnes of fossil carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions this year" (ucdavis.edu/climate/blog/fossil-fuel-co2-emissions-hit-record-high-2025). 2035 and 2050: IEA World Energy Outlook 2025, Stated Policies Scenario, energy CO2 "just over 38 Gt" at the peak, about 35 Gt in the mid-2030s and "below 30 Gt" in 2050 (iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2025/stated-policies-scenario, read from a search summary: the IEA page returned 403). A straight line between the points, and the 2050 value held after 2050, are ours (stopgap SG-NATION-climate-world-path).

landUseCo2GtPerYear.source: Global Carbon Budget 2024, Earth System Science Data 17:965 (2025): land-use change 4.2 +/- 2.6 GtCO2 a year, held flat.

usShareOfFossil.source: 4.789 GtCO2 (EIA, 2024) over 37.4 GtCO2 of global fossil CO2 (Global Carbon Budget 2024), held at the 2024 share along the path.
